symptom: ako/mxcli#1917 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1723): after `run --local --test-endpoint --detach` and `run stop` on Windows the project kept module MxTest, AfterStartupMicroflow 'MxTest.RegisterEndpoint', themesource/mxtest/ and javasource/mxtest/ — git status dirty, and once MxTest was dropped the next build failed CE1613 on the after-startup. Reported success throughout.
cause: The endpoint is removed only by HostedEndpoint.Remove inside the dev-loop process (a defer and the os.Exit path). On Windows terminateProcess is `taskkill /T /F` — the code comment even said the teardown does not run — so a detached run never got to Remove; on any platform a SIGKILL after stopGrace or a crash skipped it too. Nothing outside the process knew what to undo.
file: cmd/mxcli/testrunner/host_restore.go (restore record + RestoreAbandonedEndpoint), cmd/mxcli/testrunner/host.go (record written before install, removed by Remove, stale one cleaned before a new install), cmd/mxcli/cmd_run_lifecycle.go (runStop restores after the process is gone)
insight: Teardown that lives in a process's exit path needs a durable record the moment it has something to undo, because a stop the process cannot see (taskkill /F, SIGKILL, crash) is a normal stop on one platform. The record carries the pre-install .mpr bytes and tree digest so the cross-process restore is as byte-exact as the in-process one, and it is gated on the owner PID being dead so a live run's endpoint is never pulled. The Windows bug reproduces on Linux by SIGKILL-ing the detached run before `run stop` — that is what taskkill /F is — so the integration test runs where mxbuild does; the graceful SIGTERM stop is the control (it already restored). Revert proof: a binary with only the runStop call stubbed fails the killed-run phase with the reported leftovers; beware a stub that does not compile (unused import) — the test then fails in 9 s for the wrong reason. The second half of the issue (dist/pages 404 after `test --attach`) is a separate cause: runAttached's applyModelChange calls serve.Build directly, bypassing the bundler/serve-recovery path the run's own reload uses; reproduced on Linux 11.12.6.
